$comment: Shared behavioural contract for money formatting.
The website computes these in TypeScript (src/lib/money.ts) and the Flutter
app computes them in Dart (lib/format/money.dart). Dart cannot import
TypeScript, so the two implementations are proven identical by asserting
both against this file rather than by sharing code.
Both test suites read it: src/lib/money.contract.test.ts here, and
test/money_contract_test.dart in the app repo. If you change a formatting
rule, change it here first and watch both suites fail.
The copy in the app repo is kept in sync by scripts/sync-contracts.mjs.

format.why: A free consultation type is legal and must not render as $0.00.
Opera gloves — the cheapest catalogue item.
Leading zero in the cents must survive.

formatRange.why: Em dash U+2014 with a space either side. A hyphen reads as a typo at display sizes.
Degenerate range still renders both ends.

gstComponent.why: GST on a $110 total is $10, not $11. Divide by 11, never multiply by 0.1.
Rounds to nearest; a one cent total has no GST component.

exGst.why: exGst + gst must equal the total exactly.

instalment.why: Rounds UP. Rounding to nearest quoted four instalments summing below the total, which is a promise the checkout then breaks.
